PRODUCT DATA SHEET: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: PRODUCT DATA SHEET, edition not printed (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/n/sikatack_panel-10.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide PRODUCT DATA SHEET where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (edition not printed).
1.2 Product description. Refer to manufacturer. This is not stated in the data sheet reviewed (edition not printed).
1.3 Intended uses. Refer to manufacturer. This is not stated in the data sheet reviewed (edition not printed).

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. PRODUCT DATA SHEET
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (edition not printed) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - CQP001-1: Sika internal procedure reference, not a published standard. Where:  > PRODUCT DATA SHEET (p.1).
    - CQP019-1: Sika internal procedure reference, not a published standard. Where:  > PRODUCT DATA SHEET (p.1).
    - CQP049-1: Sika internal procedure reference, not a published standard. Where:  > PRODUCT DATA SHEET (p.1).
    - ISO 527: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where:  > PRODUCT DATA SHEET (p.1).
    - CQP023-1: Sika internal procedure reference, not a published standard. Where:  > PRODUCT DATA SHEET (p.1).
    - CQP036-1: Sika internal procedure reference, not a published standard. Where:  > PRODUCT DATA SHEET (p.1).
    - CQP045-1: Sika internal procedure reference, not a published standard. Where:  > PRODUCT DATA SHEET (p.1).
    - CQP509-1: Sika internal procedure reference, not a published standard. Where:  > PRODUCT DATA SHEET (p.1).
    - CQP513-1: Sika internal procedure reference, not a published standard. Where:  > PRODUCT DATA SHEET (p.1).

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 Substrate preparation. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (edition not printed) states no substrate preparation requirements.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (edition not printed) and the requirements below.
4.2 . 1-component polyurethane for panel bonding in ventilated facades TYPICAL PRODUCT DATA (FURTHER VALUES SEE SAFETY DATA SHEET); Chemical base 1-component polyurethane Colour (CQP001-1) Grey Cure mechanism Moisture-curing Density (uncured) 1.3 kg/l Non-sag properties Good Application temperature
    - 1-component product, ready to use
    - Weathering resistant
    - Bonds well to a wide variety of substrates AREAS OF APPLICATION SikaTack® Panel-10 is suitable for structural joints in ventilated facades and cladded interior walls between the vertically installed substructure and the facade panel that will be subjected to dynamic and static stresses. Suitable substrates are anodized and coated aluminum, metal composite, high pressure laminate and ceramic materials. This product is suitable for experienced professional users only. Tests with actual substrates and conditions have to be performed to ensure adhesion and material compatibility.
    - Safety Data Sheets
    - General Guideline SikaTack® Panel System PACKAGING INFORMATION
    | ambient | 5 ─ 40 °C |
    | CQP = Corporate Quality Procedure | A) 23 °C / 50 % r. h. |
    | DESCRIPTION | PRODUCT BENEFITS |
    | SikaTack® Panel-10 is a non-sag, 1-component polyurethane of paste-like consistency for structural joints in ventilated facades and interior wall cladding between the vertically installed substructure and the panel that will be subjected to dynamic and static stresses. It cures on exposure to atmospheric humidity. SikaTack® Panel-10 is part of the SikaTack® Panel system for the economic, concealed fixing of ventilated facades. | Elastic fixing system, vibration and movement absorbing Provides creative opportunities for facade design Uniform tension over the whole facade panel (no stress points) |
    | CURE MECHANISM | To avoid condensation on the surfaces, the |
    | SikaTack® Panel-10 cures by reaction with atmospheric moisture. At low temperatures the water content of the air is generally lower and the curing reaction proceeds some-what slower (see diagram 1). | temperature of the bonding components (e.g. façade panels, sub-frames) must be at least 3 °C higher than the dew point of the air. The skin time is significantly shorter in hot and humid climate. The panel must always be installed within 75 % of the skin time determined under local climate conditions (see General Guideline “SikaTack® Panel System”). Never join bonding parts if the adhesive has formed a skin. SikaTack® Panel-10 can be processed with hand, pneumatic or electric driven piston guns. |
    | Diagram 1: Curing speed SikaTack® Panel-10 |
    | METHOD OF APPLICATION |
    | Surface preparation |
    | Surfaces must be clean, dry and free from grease, oil, dust and contaminants. Surface treatment depends on the specific nature of the substrates and is crucial for a long lasting bond. |
    | Application |
    | The standard geometry for bonding façade panels is at least 12 x 3 mm. The supplied nozzle (10 x 8 mm) ensures proper dimension of the compressed bead (see figure below). |
    | Figure 1: Recommended bead configuration |
    | The optimum temperature for substrate and adhesive is between 15 °C and 25 °C. Do not apply at temperatures below 5 °C or above 40 °C. |
    | Unipack | 600 ml |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Skin time (CQP019-1) 60 minutes A Curing speed (CQP049-1) (See diagram)
    Shore A hardness (CQP023-1 / ISO 48-4) 40 Tensile strength (CQP036-1 / ISO 527) 1.8 MPa Elongation at break (CQP036-1 / ISO 527) 500 % Tear propagation resistance (CQP045-1 / ISO 34) 7 N/mm Service temperature (CQP509-1 / CQP513-1) -40 ─ 90 °C Shelf life 12 months B
    B) Storage below 25 °C
    Removal Uncured SikaTack® Panel-10 can be removed from tools and equipment with Sika® Remover-208 or another suitable solvent. Once cured, the material can only be removed mechanically. Hands and exposed skin have to be washed immediately using hand wipes such as Sika® Cleaner-350H or a suitable industrial hand cleaner and water. Do not use solvents on skin. Application limits SikaTack® Panel-10 used for panel bonding is always used in conjunction with SikaTack® Panel Fixing Tape. SikaTack® Panel Fixing Tape ensures the correct joint thickness and keeps the bonded panels initially in place. By curing, SikaTack® Panel-10 builds up strength and takes over the long-term load bearing. SikaTack® Panel Fixing Tape is not a structural component. FURTHER INFORMATION The information herein is offered for general guidance only. Advice on specific applications is available on request from the Technical Department of Sika Industry. Copies of the following publications are available on request:
    BASIS OF PRODUCT DATA All technical data stated in this document are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control. HEALTH AND SAFETY INFORMATION For information and advice regarding transportation, handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the actual Safety Data Sheets containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data. DISCLAIMER The information, and, in particular, the recommendations relating to the application and enduse of Sika products, are given in good faith based on Sika's current knowledge and experience of the products when properly stored, handled and applied under normal conditions in accordance with Sika's recommendations. In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered. The user of the product must test the product's suitability for the intended application and purpose. Sika reserves the right to change the properties of its products. The proprietary rights of third parties must be observed. All orders are accepted subject to our current terms of sale and delivery. Users must always refer to the most recent issue of the local Product Data Sheet for the product concerned, copies of which will be supplied on request.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, confirm the site conditions with the manufacturer. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Conditions to be verified. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (edition not printed) lists no application condition limits.
5.3 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: PRODUCT DATA SHEET, edition not printed, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/n/sikatack_panel-10.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS SikaTack® Panel-10, version 13/02/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/k/sds-sikatack-panel-10.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SikaTack Panel 10, version 13/05/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/t/MSDS%20SikaTack%20Panel%20-%2010%20GHS7.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. Refer to manufacturer. This is not stated in the data sheet reviewed (edition not printed).
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.

The proprietary rights of third parties must be observed. All orders are accepted subject to our current terms of sale and delivery. Users must always refer to the most recent issue of the local Product Data Sheet for the product concerned, copies of which will be supplied on request.
6.4 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.1, and include the records in the project documentation.
